packet.headline_seed: Tulsi Gabbard to resign as US director of national intelligence
packet.description_seed: Gabbard who has been largely out of public view during recent US operations says she is leaving due to her husband's illness.

what: Tulsi Gabbard to resign as US director of national intelligence

clean_source_blocks.text: Gabbard who has been largely out of public view during recent US operations says she is leaving due to her husband's illness.

Tulsi Gabbard has now shared a statement on X, confirming that she is resigning from her post as national intelligence director, citing her husband’s illness. In a resignation letter first reported by Fox News, Gabbard tells the president she is “deeply grateful for the trust you placed in me and for the opportunity to lead the Office of the Director of National Intelligence for the last year and a half.” “Unfortunately, I must submit my resignation, effective June 30, 2026. My husband, Abraham, has recently been diagnosed with an extremely rare form of bone cancer.” Her husband “faces major challenges in the coming weeks and months”, she wrote. “At this time, I must step away from public service to be by his side and fully support him through this battle.” ---

Tulsi Gabbard will resign from her position as the US director of national intelligence in the Trump administration, citing her husband's recent bone cancer diagnosis. "His strength and love have sustained me through every challenge," she wrote in her resignation letter obtained by CBS News, the BBC's US partner. "I cannot in good conscience ask him to face this fight alone while I continue in this demanding and time-consuming position." President Donald Trump said in a social media post that Gabbard "has done an incredible job, and we will miss her". Her resignation is effective 30 June. Aaron Lukas, the principal deputy director, will step in as acting director, Trump said.

See more of our coverage in your search results. WASHINGTON — Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard submitted her resignation Friday — citing her husband’s recent cancer diagnosis. Gabbard, a longtime skeptic of US intervention overseas, apparently did not cite the ongoing Iran war in a resignation letter first reported by Fox News Digital. “Unfortunately, I must submit my resignation, effective June 30, 2026,” she wrote. “My husband, Abraham, has recently been diagnosed with an extremely rare form of bone cancer.” The former Hawaii Democratic congresswoman also thanked President Trump for “the trust you placed in me.” Follow The Post’s live coverage of President Trump and national politics for the latest news and analysis

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Tulsi Gabbard will resign from her position as the US director of national intelligence in the Trump administration, citing her husband's recent bone cancer diagnosis.

"His strength and love have sustained me through every challenge," she wrote in her resignation letter obtained by CBS News, the BBC's US partner. "I cannot in good conscience ask him to face this fight alone while I continue in this demanding and time-consuming position."

President Donald Trump said in a social media post that Gabbard "has done an incredible job, and we will miss her".

Her resignation is effective 30 June. Aaron Lukas, the principal deputy director, will step in as acting director, Trump said.

Gabbard, a loyal supporter of Trump during his 2024 presidential campaign, was confirmed as one of the most powerful figures in US intelligence-gathering weeks after he returned to the White House in 2025. But this year, she has largely been out of public view as the US has taken military action against Iran, put pressure on Cuba, and notably removed Venezuela's president.

Gabbard is the latest Cabinet member to leave the Trump administration after  Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and Attorney General Pam Bondi both left the administration earlier this year. She becomes the fourth cabinet member to leave; Lori Chavez-DeRemer left her position as labor secretary in April.

In her resignation letter, Gabbard said her husband, Abraham, "faces major challenges in the coming weeks and months."

Trump posted on social media that Gabbard "rightfully, wants to be with him, bringing him back to good health as they currently fight a tough battle together. I have no doubt he will soon be better than ever."

During her political career, she has positioned herself as an anti-interventionalist in  foreign wars, creating tension after Trump decided to enter a war with Iran. Following US-Israel strikes on Iran, she avoided endorsing the decision, carefully evading questions during a congressional hearing in March about whether the administration knew of the conflict's potential fallout.

She also faced scrutiny during questioning over what Democrats perceived as  discrepancies between the White House's and intelligence community's claims about Iran's nuclear enrichment capabilities.

Under her leadership, the intelligence community has reduced in size, and has been marked by allegations she concealed intelligence from Congress and politicized the office.

---

[Lähde: The Guardian]
Tulsi Gabbard has now shared a statement on X, confirming that she is resigning from her post as national intelligence director, citing her husband’s illness.

In a resignation letter first reported by Fox News, Gabbard tells the president she is “deeply grateful for the trust you placed in me and for the opportunity to lead the Office of the Director of National Intelligence for the last year and a half.”

“Unfortunately, I must submit my resignation, effective June 30, 2026. My husband, Abraham, has recently been diagnosed with an extremely rare form of bone cancer.”

Her husband “faces major challenges in the coming weeks and months”, she wrote. “At this time, I must step away from public service to be by his side and fully support him through this battle.”

---

[Lähde: New York Post]
See more of our coverage in your search results.

WASHINGTON — Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard submitted her resignation Friday — citing her husband’s recent cancer diagnosis.

Gabbard, a longtime skeptic of US intervention overseas, apparently did not cite the ongoing Iran war in a resignation letter first reported by Fox News Digital.

“Unfortunately, I must submit my resignation, effective June 30, 2026,” she wrote. “My husband, Abraham, has recently been diagnosed with an extremely rare form of bone cancer.”

The former Hawaii Democratic congresswoman also thanked President Trump for “the trust you placed in me.”

Follow The Post’s live coverage of President Trump and national politics for the latest news and analysis

The news broke within minutes of the president saying he plans to remain at the White House this weekend — rather than at his New Jersey golf course — fueling speculation he’s poised to resume attacks on the Islamic Republic.

Gabbard has publicly remained loyal to Trump during Operation Epic Fury, testifying to the Senate in March that “the intelligence community assessed that Iran maintained the intention to rebuild and to continue to grow their nuclear enrichment capability.”

But she has rarely been at the forefront of the administration — with Trump often singling out and praising CIA Director John Ratcliffe for his contributions.

Gabbard had aligned with Trump on other priorities, including investigating alleged vote fraud in the 2020 election.

Her departure follows the fiery resignation in March of her former subordinate Joe Kent, the onetime head of the National Counterterrorism Center, who claimed Israel had duped Trump into attacking Iran.

payload.title: Tulsi Gabbard eroaa Yhdysvaltain kansallisen tiedustelun johdosta
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltain kansallisen tiedustelun johtaja Tulsi Gabbard jättää tehtävänsä 30. kesäkuuta 2026. Hän perustelee päätöstä puolisonsa Abrahamin erittäin harvinaisella luusyöpädiagnoosilla.
payload.content:
Tulsi Gabbard eroaa Yhdysvaltain kansallisen tiedustelun johtajan tehtävästä presidentti Donald Trumpin hallinnossa. Gabbardin mukaan päätöksen taustalla on hänen puolisonsa Abrahamin hiljattain saama erittäin harvinaisen luusyövän diagnoosi, jonka vuoksi hän haluaa vetäytyä julkisesta palveluksesta ja olla puolisonsa tukena. Ero tulee voimaan 30. kesäkuuta 2026.

## Puolison sairaus ratkaisi päätöksen

Gabbard vahvisti eronsa X:ssä julkaisemassaan lausunnossa. Lähteiden mukaan erokirjeen raportoi ensin Fox News, ja siinä Gabbard kiitti presidenttiä luottamuksesta sekä mahdollisuudesta johtaa kansallisen tiedustelun johtajan virastoa viimeisen puolentoista vuoden ajan.

Kirjeessä Gabbard kirjoitti, että hänen puolisonsa Abraham on saanut erittäin harvinaisen luusyöpädiagnoosin. Hän kuvasi puolison olevan suurten haasteiden edessä tulevina viikkoina ja kuukausina. Gabbardin mukaan hän ei voi hyvällä omallatunnolla pyytää Abrahamia kohtaamaan sairautta yksin samalla, kun hän itse jatkaisi vaativassa ja aikaa vievässä tehtävässä.

Gabbard sanoi astuvansa sivuun julkisesta palveluksesta voidakseen olla puolisonsa rinnalla ja tukea häntä sairauden aikana. BBC:n mukaan Gabbard on ollut viimeaikaisten Yhdysvaltain operaatioiden aikana suurelta osin poissa julkisuudesta.

## Trump kiitti ja nimesi väliaikaisen johtajan

Presidentti Donald Trump kommentoi Gabbardin lähtöä sosiaalisessa mediassa. Trumpin mukaan Gabbard on tehnyt erinomaista työtä, ja hänen panostaan tullaan kaipaamaan.

Trumpin mukaan kansallisen tiedustelun johtajan viraston pääasiallinen apulaisjohtaja Aaron Lukas siirtyy väliaikaiseksi johtajaksi Gabbardin eron jälkeen. Näin viraston johto vaihtuu, kun Gabbardin ero astuu voimaan kesäkuun lopussa.

## Taustalla ei mainittu Iranin sotaa

New York Postin mukaan Gabbard ei ilmeisesti yhdistänyt erokirjeessään päätöstään meneillään olevaan Iranin sotaan. Päätöksen perusteluna esitettiin puolison sairaus ja tarve olla hänen tukenaan.

Gabbard on aiemmin toiminut Havaijin demokraattiedustajana kongressissa. Hänet tunnetaan myös pitkäaikaisena Yhdysvaltain ulkomaisiin sotilaallisiin interventioihin kriittisesti suhtautuneena poliitikkona.
summary_bullets: Tulsi Gabbard eroaa Yhdysvaltain kansallisen tiedustelun johtajan tehtävästä.
Gabbard perustelee päätöstä puolisonsa Abrahamin erittäin harvinaisella luusyöpädiagnoosilla.
Aaron Lukas toimii Trumpin mukaan väliaikaisena johtajana.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu packetin usean lähteen tietoihin. Keskeiset varmistetut asiat ovat ero, voimaantulopäivä, perhesyy ja väliaikaiseksi johtajaksi nimetty Aaron Lukas. Puolison sairauden tarkka diagnoosi on käsitelty vain lähteissä esitetyllä tasolla.
